Current checkout audit · 2026-06-30 · Canonical feature and user-story ledger

2 confirmed defect groups: compact-screen multiline editors lacked a reliable keyboard dismissal path, and the iOS UI harness had drifted from the active 5 x 5 decision-matrix Orders surface. Both were fixed and all 29 UI tests now pass.

External limitations: credentialed live OpenRouter/Z.AI/Turso calls were not sent; a full human VoiceOver traversal remains manual. Deterministic routing, parsing, persistence, accessibility-tree, and reduced-motion paths passed.
Primary evidence: script/lint.sh; full macOS XCTest (133 passed, 2 credential skips); full iOS UI suite (29 passed); generic iOS test build; build_and_run.sh --verify; workbook formula and visual QA.
Active product scope: Apple/. Legacy web/server material is reference-only; no service worker applies to the native product. F021, F040, and F051 were reconciled to current code.

As a player planning a turn, I want a complete matrix of legal decisions for the current world state, So that I can choose strategic actions without being offered impossible or stale options.

The Orders surface shows exactly 25 unique cells across Economy, Society, Diplomacy, Security, and Sovereignty rows and Stabilize, Prepare, Cooperate, Project, and Transform columns. Every cell is concrete, affordable, valid for the current state fingerprint, and preserves cost, action kind, mechanics, targets, and structured sovereignty intent. Loading, provider failure, legacy-board recovery, refresh, duplicate rejection, queued state, and empty state remain visible.

As a player playing as a democracy or autocracy, I want relationships between nations of similar ideologies to improve over time and relationships between differing ideologies to decay over time, So that geopolitical blocs form naturally.

AI drift updates relationship scores between countries: nations with same government types drift positive (+0.05 per month), whereas democracy vs autocracy relationships drift negative (-0.1 per month).
Run AI drift drift logic over 12 months; assert democracy-democracy relationship rises and democracy-autocracy decays.

As a player running a democracy, I want periodic democratic elections to occur based on my country's next election round, So that my continuation in power depends on public approval, with low approval leading to opposition victories, policy/doctrine shifts (for AI), and stability hits.

When current round reaches nextElectionRound for a democracy, an election is resolved. Win chance is equal to public approval. Opposition victory resets approval to 55%, sets next election in 48 rounds, shifts AI doctrine and budget priority, and imposes a -5 stability hit on the player country.
Trigger advance turn past nextElectionRound; check for logged election events in timeline, next election round updates, and stability delta on opposition win.

As a player running an autocracy, I want critically low regime support to trigger potential coup attempts, So that unstable autocracies risk overthrow, causing severe stability drops, policy shifts, and decayed relations with democracies.

Autocracies with regime support below 25% have a 30% chance per month of a coup. A coup causes a -15 stability hit for players, resets support to 45%, shifts AI country doctrine to defensive/isolationist, resets budget to stability, and decays relations with democracies by -40.
Set autocracy approval to 15%; run simulateAIDrift multiple turns; check that coup fires, logs a timeline event, decays relations with democracies, and reduces player stability.

As a player advancing the campaign, I want every non-player government to make reproducible independent decisions, So that the world evolves coherently and the same saved campaign can be replayed.

On every completed turn, every non-player country chooses one bounded action from its own 5 x 5 Economy/Society/Diplomacy/Security/Sovereignty matrix. Campaign, country, turn, persistent 12-bit policy profile, and decision-step seeds make choices replayable and schedule-independent. The highest-salience choices become individual target-dated events, lower-salience choices become one aggregate world event, relationship/agenda state persists, and stored insurgency/cooperation pressure can produce structured secession or merger events without mutating unrelated player state.

As a player occupying another country, I want that country's allies to react diplomatically, So that territorial aggression has coherent relationship costs.

For each foreign region occupied by the player, AI countries with a relationship above 50 to the defender reduce their relationship with the player by a bounded monthly penalty before normal ideological drift.
Create a player occupation and an AI ally of the defender; simulate one month; verify the ally relationship with the player falls by the occupation penalty and remains clamped.

The source loop identified allies and read the current score but never wrote the penalty, so occupations produced no allied reaction. The relationship mutation is now applied and covered by a focused test.
Defender allies did not penalize the player after foreign occupation because the calculated relationship score was discarded.
Apply the bounded monthly relationship penalty back to each qualifying ally state and added deterministic coverage.

Focused allied-occupation test passes; full macOS XCTest passes.
